intro: Each post belongs to one of four angles and carries a short topic tag. The budget is how many posts each angle gets. Cadence: two posts a week, Tuesday and Thursday. October is a little fuller than usual because it includes two short demo videos, one on Dashcam View and one on the custom dashboard.

waitingOn.ask: Approve “Sell to the person with the problem” in Ordinal. The request has been open since August.
Confirm Rich and Mike are happy to be tagged, and whether we can name the spraying operation in “I didn't miss any spots.”

angles.name: Playbook
angles.why: Four this month, two of them the new feature demo videos.
angles.description: How you actually do the work, broken down so a reader could run it tomorrow.
angles.forYou: How fleets actually get value from the platform: selling to the person with the problem, pulling proof fast when a claim lands, a first screen built for your morning, and pricing that matches the season.

angles.name: Proof
angles.why: One customer story from Rich's session.
angles.description: Specific outcomes and the story behind them, with the numbers and the messy middle left in.
angles.forYou: Customers using Razor in ways the team didn't plan for, told through Rich's stories from the field.

angles.name: Stance
angles.why: Two, one early and one late in the month.
angles.description: What you believe about where your industry is going, stated plainly enough to be disagreed with.
angles.forYou: Your read on AI and software: most of the buzz fades, and the fastest releases come from slowing down to rebuild first.

angles.name: Human
angles.description: The person behind the company: what you're learning, deciding, and getting wrong.
angles.forYou: The people behind Razor and the standard they set for customers.
